livelihood_summary: Agro-pastoral: rain-fed cultivation and cattle, with fishing, hunting and wild foods; known deficit production area
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Mar-Oct (May-Nov by rainfall); land preparation Jan-Feb; planting Apr-Jun; weeding Jun-Aug; harvest Aug-Nov; lean season May-Jul; livestock migration Dec-Apr; fishing year-round
main_hazards: Flooding annually Jul-Oct; livestock disease May-Nov; crop pests Jun-Sep; drought once in three years; cattle raiding Feb-May
coping_and_notes: Own cereal now lasts 2-4 months instead of 9; poor households sell charcoal, firewood, goats and labor; Sobat and Nile are central to seasonal livestock movement
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, SS06 (p.28-30)

livelihood_summary: Fishing, rain-fed cropping, livestock and wild foods on a narrow swampy floodplain along the Nile; river ports critical for trade
main_crops: Sorghum (staple), maize, cowpeas, groundnuts, vegetables (okra, pumpkins)
seasonal_calendar: Fishing year-round, lowest in the rains when swamps and lakes are fished; land preparation Feb-Mar; harvest Sep-Nov; vegetables in dry season; livestock sales Feb-Jul; fish sales Jan-Apr and Aug-Nov
main_hazards: Flooding every 3-5 years plus annual river rise; crop pests; livestock disease; localized cattle raiding
coping_and_notes: Sorghum harvest normally lasts 6-7 months, now 2-4 months; poor households sell fish, firewood, papyrus mats, brew; many households retreat into swamp for fish and wild foods
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, SS08 (p.35-37)

zone_name: North-western Nile basin cattle and maize
livelihood_summary: Livestock-focused agro-pastoral; maize is main staple; fishing and wild foods; deficit cereal producer relying on trade
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season May-Nov; floods Jul-Aug; dry spell May-Jun; livestock disease peaks Feb-Apr; fishing mostly in dry season
main_hazards: Floods Jul-Aug; dry spell May-Jun; bird plagues; Striga and fall armyworm; livestock disease; dry-season cattle raiding
coping_and_notes: Poor households may buy up to 9 months of staple needs instead of 2-3; sell goats, sheep, labor and bush products
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, SS09 (p.38-39)
